title: Add magic-link login
summary: Users can sign in by entering their email and clicking a one-time link, instead of using a password. Passwords keep working for now. The link is single-use, expires, and is tied to the browser that asked for it.
goal: A user who enters their email on `/login` receives a link, clicks it within the expiry window, and lands signed in on `/dashboard` — with no password involved.
non_goals: Removing password login (separate plan once usage data is in)
Changing the session cookie format in `src/lib/session.ts`
context: Next.js 14 app router, Postgres via Prisma (`prisma/schema.prisma`), sessions in `src/lib/session.ts` using signed cookies.
Email goes out through `src/lib/email.ts`, which wraps Postmark (checked `package.json`: `postmark@4.0.2`).

assumptions.text: Every user row has a verified email, so a link can go to any existing account.
assumptions.basis: `User.emailVerifiedAt` is non-null for all rows in the seed data, but I could not check production.

assumptions.text: Postmark's sandbox server is fine for local development; no new email provider is needed.
assumptions.basis: `.env.example` has `POSTMARK_TOKEN` and `src/lib/email.ts` already sends the password-reset email.

assumptions.text: Rate limiting can reuse the existing `rateLimit()` helper in `src/lib/rate-limit.ts`.
assumptions.basis: It already guards `/api/auth/password` (5 attempts per 15 minutes per IP).

questions.text: How long should a login link stay valid?
questions.why: Sets `MAGIC_LINK_TTL_MINUTES` and the wording in the email. Shorter is safer; longer survives slow inboxes.

options.label: 10 minutes
options.detail: Tight. Some corporate mail filters delay longer.

options.label: 1 hour
options.detail: Most forgiving; higher risk if the inbox is shared.

questions.text: What should happen when someone enters an email that has no account?
questions.why: Decides whether `/api/auth/magic-link` can reveal which emails are registered.

options.label: Show the same 'check your email' message
options.detail: Doesn't reveal who has an account. Nothing is sent.

options.label: Send a sign-up link instead
options.detail: Friendlier, but creates a new sign-up path to test.

options.label: Say 'no account with that email'
options.detail: Clearest, but lets anyone check which emails are registered.

decisions.title: Where to store login tokens
decisions.context: A token is created per request, read once on click, then deleted. Expected volume is low (hundreds a day).

options.label: New `LoginToken` table in Postgres
pros: Works in tests with the existing test DB
cons: Needs a cleanup job for expired rows

options.label: Redis with a TTL
options.detail: Key per token, expires on its own.
cons: Redis isn't in the stack yet: new service, new env vars, new failure mode

steps.title: Add the `LoginToken` model and migration
steps.detail: Store only a SHA-256 hash of the token, never the token itself. `browserNonce` ties the link to the browser that requested it.

files.what: Add `model LoginToken { id, tokenHash @unique, userId, expiresAt, browserNonce, createdAt }` with a relation to `User`.
Generated by the command below; commit it.

done_when: `pnpm prisma migrate status` reports no pending migrations

steps.title: Write token helpers with tests
steps.detail: `createLoginToken(userId)` returns the raw token and stores its hash. `consumeLoginToken(raw, nonce)` returns the user id if the hash exists, is not expired, and the nonce matches; it deletes the row in the same transaction either way.

files.what: Cases: valid, expired, wrong nonce, reused, unknown token.

done_when: A consumed token cannot be consumed a second time (test asserts `null` on reuse)

steps.title: Add the request endpoint `POST /api/auth/magic-link`
steps.detail: Body: `{ email }`. Always responds `200 { ok: true }` (see q2). Sets an HTTP-only `mlnonce` cookie (10-minute max-age) and, if the user exists, emails the link `/auth/verify?token=…`. Rate-limited with `rateLimit('magic-link', ip, 5, '15m')`.

files.what: Validate email with zod, rate-limit, create token, send email.
Email template: one button, plain-text fallback, expiry sentence.

done_when: `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/magic-link -d '{"email":"demo@example.com"}'` returns 200 and a message appears in the Postmark sandbox
The 6th request from one IP within 15 minutes returns 429

steps.title: Add the verify page `/auth/verify`
steps.detail: Server component reads `token` from the query and `mlnonce` from cookies, calls `consumeLoginToken`, then calls the existing `createSession(userId)` and redirects to `/dashboard`. On failure it renders one page that says the link is invalid or expired, with a button back to `/login`.

files.what: Consume token, create session, redirect; failure state.

done_when: Clicking a fresh link signs you in and lands on `/dashboard`
Clicking the same link again shows the 'invalid or expired' page
Opening the link in a different browser shows the 'invalid or expired' page

steps.title: Add the email option to the login page
steps.detail: Add an "Email me a link" form above the password form. After submit, swap the form for a "Check your email" panel (see the mock above). Password login stays below a divider.

files.what: Client component: email field, submit, sent state, error state.

done_when: Playwright test `e2e/magic-link.spec.ts` passes: request link → read it from the Postmark sandbox → land on `/dashboard`

steps.title: Purge expired tokens nightly
steps.detail: Reuse the existing cron route pattern from `src/app/api/cron/cleanup-sessions/route.ts`.

files.what: Calls `purgeExpiredTokens()`; protected by `CRON_SECRET` like the sessions job.

done_when: Calling the route with the cron secret deletes rows where `expiresAt < now()` and returns the count

risks.text: Email scanners (e.g. Outlook Safe Links) pre-open links and burn the single-use token.
risks.mitigation: The verify page needs a click ("Continue to sign in") before consuming the token, so a bot's GET doesn't use it up.

risks.text: The nonce cookie is lost if the user requests on desktop and opens the email on their phone.
risks.mitigation: The failure page explains this case and offers to send a new link to the current device.

verification: Fresh account: request a link, click it, land on `/dashboard` signed in
Same link twice: second click shows the expired page
`pnpm test && pnpm playwright test` pass with no new warnings

sections.title: Rollout
sections.body: Ship behind `FEATURE_MAGIC_LINK` (env flag, default off). Turn it on for staff accounts first, then everyone after one week with no auth errors in the logs.
items: Day 0: deploy with the flag off

output_hint.why: This session has used most of its context on research; a fresh session will build more reliably.
